item.aggregated_output:
name: CI

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
  # Run the full workflow on push to main so the pre-commit hook-env
  # cache populates under the default-branch scope. PRs from feature
  # branches can read default-branch caches but cannot read each
  # other's, so without this trigger every fresh PR pays the
  # ~1m 40s cold-install cost on the lint job. The cost of running
  # all jobs on each merge to main is accepted as a side effect.
  # Issue #1034.
  push:
    branches:
      - main

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Force all JavaScript-based actions (including transitive sub-actions like
  # the actions/cache@v4 carried inside actions/setup-node and
  # actions/setup-python) to run under Node.js 24.  Suppresses the deprecation
  # warning that fires on every job:
  #   "Node.js 20 actions are deprecated."
  # Per GitHub release notes 2025-09-19, Node 20 is removed from runners on
  # 2026-09-16; this env var becomes the default on 2026-06-02.
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: "true"

jobs:
  # External-tool linters only: markdownlint, jsonlint, and actionlint.
  # All local bash/python linters run in the parallel `lint-local` job.
  # `agent-lint`, `agnix`, and `shellcheck` run in their dedicated jobs.
  # `gitleaks` working-tree scan moved to the `gitleaks` job to shed ~40s
  # from this job's critical path. Test harnesses run in the separate
  # `test-harnesses` job. Mermaid fence lint and SIGPIPE safety lint run in
  # the parallel `lint-mermaid` job (closes #2080).
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: .github/workflows/requirements-lint.txt
      - uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pre-commit
          key: pre-commit-${{ hashFiles('.pre-commit-config.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            pre-commit-
      - name: Install lint dependencies
        env:
          PIP_RETRIES: "5"
          PIP_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT: "30"
        run: pip install -r .github/workflows/requirements-lint.txt
      - name: Run pre-commit linters (external tools)
        # Runs markdownlint, jsonlint, and actionlint only.
        # `agent-lint`, `agnix`, and `shellcheck` run in dedicated jobs.
        # `gitleaks` moved to the `gitleaks` job. Local bash/python linters
        # run in `lint-local`. If a dedicated job is removed, drop its hook
        # name from SKIP to restore CI coverage. Issue #1034.
        env:
          SKIP: agnix,lint-mermaid-fences,shellcheck,gitleaks,agent-lint,lint-skill-invocations,lint-literal-counts,lint-no-raw-stderr-after-quiet-init,lint-gh-body-inline,lint-bash32,bash-syntax-check,check-topology-rule-paths,lint-readability-preamble,lint-renderer-substitution-safety,lint-skill-md-flag-signature,lint-bare-grep-probe,lint-codex-exec-auth,lint-awk-multibyte-regex
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          log="$(mktemp)"
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            set +e
            make lint-only 2>&1 | tee "$log"
            rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
            set -e

            if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
              exit 0
            fi
            if ! grep -Fq 'failed to download https://github.com/zhupanov/agent-lint/releases/download/' "$log"; then
              exit "$rc"
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" -eq 3 ]; then
              exit "$rc"
            fi

            echo "agent-lint release download failed; retrying make lint-only" >&2
            sleep 10
          done

  # Local bash/python linters — split from `lint` into a parallel job so
  # both halves run concurrently. Runs lint-skill-invocations,
  # lint-literal-counts, lint-bash32, lint-renderer-substitution-safety,
  # lint-awk-multibyte-regex, and all other local hooks while `lint` runs
  # the external-tool hooks (markdownlint, jsonlint, agent-lint, actionlint).
  lint-local:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: .github/workflows/requirements-lint.txt
      - uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pre-commit
          key: pre-commit-${{ hashFiles('.pre-commit-config.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            pre-commit-
      - name: Install lint dependencies
        env:
          PIP_RETRIES: "5"
          PIP_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT: "30"
        run: pip install -r .github/workflows/requirements-lint.txt
      - name: Run pre-commit linters (local)
        # Runs only local bash/python linters. External tools (markdownlint,
        # jsonlint, actionlint) run in `lint`. Dedicated-job hooks
        # (gitleaks, agnix, shellcheck, agent-lint) are skipped here.
        env:
          SKIP: agnix,lint-mermaid-fences,shellcheck,gitleaks,markdownlint,jsonlint,agent-lint,actionlint
        run: make lint-only

  # Mermaid fence lint and SIGPIPE safety lint — split from the `lint` job
  # into a parallel job so both halves run concurrently (closes #2080).
  # Requires fetch-depth: 0 so `python3 python/cli.py lint mermaid-fences --changed-only` can
  # resolve `origin/<base>...HEAD` even on PRs whose merge base is deeper
  # than the default depth=1 shallow window.
  lint-mermaid:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          # Fetch the full history so the Python Mermaid lint
          # (`python3 python/cli.py lint mermaid-fences --changed-only`) can resolve `origin/<base>...HEAD` even on
          # PRs whose merge base is deeper than the default depth=1
          # shallow window. The prior shallow checkout could yield an
          # empty / wrong diff while the lint step still exited 0,
          # silently disabling Mermaid CI coverage (closes #1426
          # follow-up D — round-2 review).
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 'lts/*'
          cache: npm
          # Track the lockfile so a lockfile-only bump invalidates the
          # npm cache (closes #1426 follow-up FINDING_1).
          cache-dependency-path: mermaid-lint/package-lock.json
      - uses: actions/cache@v5
        id: node-modules-cache
        with:
          path: mermaid-lint/node_modules
          # Key on both package.json and package-lock.json so a
          # dependency-manifest change that doesn't update the lockfile
          # still invalidates this cache (closes #1576).
          key: node-modules-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('mermaid-lint/package.json', 'mermaid-lint/package-lock.json') }}
      - uses: actions/cache@v5
        id: puppeteer-cache
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/puppeteer
          # Mirror the cache-dependency-path key on the lockfile so the
          # Chromium cache invalidates whenever resolved Puppeteer
          # changes — even via lockfile-only bumps (closes #1426
          # follow-up FINDING_1).
          key: puppeteer-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('mermaid-lint/package-lock.json') }}
      - name: Install Mermaid CLI
        # `npm ci` installs exactly from the committed lockfile and
        # fails if the lockfile is out of sync with package.json. This
        # is the conventional CI contract — `npm install` would tolerate
        # / silently update the lockfile, defeating the purpose of
        # committing it (closes #1426 follow-up FINDING_10).
        #
        # Mermaid CLI 11.x has no --parseOnly mode, so the Python lint
        # falls back to mmdc -i ... -o ....svg, which requires
        # Puppeteer's Chromium download. The puppeteer cache above
        # restores ~/.cache/puppeteer between runs so cold downloads
        # only happen when package-lock.json changes.
        #
        # Skipped only when BOTH node_modules and Puppeteer caches hit:
        # a node_modules hit with a puppeteer miss would leave Chromium
        # absent and break the mermaid lint step (closes #1576).
        if: steps.node-modules-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true' || steps.puppeteer-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        env:
          npm_config_fetch_retries: "5"
          npm_config_fetch_retry_factor: "2"
          npm_config_fetch_retry_mintimeout: "10000"
          npm_config_fetch_retry_maxtimeout: "120000"
        run: cd mermaid-lint && npm ci
      - name: Lint Mermaid fences (changed only)
        run: python3 python/cli.py lint mermaid-fences --changed-only
      - name: Pipe SIGPIPE safety lint
        run: bash scripts/test-pipe-sigpipe-safety.sh

  # Dedicated shellcheck jobs — split into `scripts` and `skills/.claude`
  # scopes running in parallel to halve wall-clock time. Each scope installs
  # the pinned shellcheck-py==0.11.0.1 binary directly (no pre-commit
  # overhead) and runs shellcheck -x in parallel via xargs. The pre-commit
  # `shellcheck` hook remains active for local `pre-commit run` and the dev
  # git-hook; CI skips it in `lint` and `lint-local` via the SKIP env var.
  # shellcheck-py pinned to 0.11.0.1 — keep in sync with .pre-commit-config.yaml on bump.
  shellcheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - scope: scripts
            paths: scripts
          - scope: skills
            paths: "skills .claude"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6

# CI splits `lint` into `lint-only` (pre-commit) and `test-harnesses`
# (regression harnesses). `lint` remains the local-dev convenience target
# that runs both, defined in terms of the two split targets to prevent drift.
lint: test-harnesses lint-bash32 lint-readability-preamble lint-renderer-substitution-safety lint-skill-md-flag-signature lint-bare-grep-probe lint-codex-exec-auth lint-awk-multibyte-regex lint-retired-scripts lint-only

py-lint:
	@$(PYTHON) -c 'import sys; raise SystemExit(0 if sys.version_info >= (3, 11) else 1)' \
		|| (printf '%s\n' "ERROR: make py-lint requires Python 3.11 or newer (PYTHON=$(PYTHON))" >&2; exit 1)
	# pylint runs with all cores when the host supports the required process-pool
	# semaphore query. Some restricted local sandboxes deny that query, so they
	# fall back to a single worker. duplicate-code is disabled here (.pylintrc)
	# and runs single-process in py-lint-duplicate-code.
	cd python && ruff check . && pylint -j $(PYLINT_JOBS) . && pyright

py-lint-duplicate-code:
	@$(PYTHON) -c 'import sys; raise SystemExit(0 if sys.version_info >= (3, 11) else 1)' \
		|| (printf '%s\n' "ERROR: make py-lint-duplicate-code requires Python 3.11 or newer (PYTHON=$(PYTHON))" >&2; exit 1)
	# Duplicate-code (R0801) runs as a dedicated single-process pass: pylint's
	# similarities checker is incorrect under -j>1 (each worker sees only a slice
	# of files), so it must run with -j 1. Kept out of `py-lint` (which disables
	# duplicate-code via .pylintrc) so the main lint pass parallelizes; this is
	# the CI `python-lint-duplicate-code` job. See issue #4480.
	cd python && pylint --disable=all --enable=duplicate-code -j 1 .

py-test:
	@$(PYTHON) -c 'import sys; raise SystemExit(0 if sys.version_info >= (3, 11) else 1)' \
		|| (printf '%s\n' "ERROR: make py-test requires Python 3.11 or newer (PYTHON=$(PYTHON))" >&2; exit 1)
	# --durations=0 emits per-test timing so CI shards (PYTEST_SHARD_ID /
	# PYTEST_SHARD_COUNT, see python/conftest.py) can be rebalanced by wall time.
	cd python && $(PYTHON) -m pytest --durations=0

lint-only:
	pre-commit run --all-files

lint-readability-preamble:
	python3 python/cli.py lint readability-preamble

lint-renderer-substitution-safety:
	bash scripts/lint-renderer-substitution-safety.sh

lint-skill-md-flag-signature:
	python3 python/cli.py lint skill-md-flag-signature

lint-bare-grep-probe:
	bash scripts/lint-bare-grep-probe.sh

lint-codex-exec-auth:
	python3 python/cli.py lint codex-exec-auth

lint-awk-multibyte-regex:
	bash scripts/lint-awk-multibyte-regex.sh

docs/linting.md:31:- **CI** — The `lint` job runs `make lint-only` (repo-wide pre-commit over all files) with `SKIP=agnix,lint-mermaid-fences,shellcheck,agent-lint` on the step, because the dedicated `agent-lint`, `agnix`, and `shellcheck` jobs run those hooks in parallel and Mermaid parsing runs as a separate changed-files step after installing the Node toolchain. A parallel `lint-mermaid` job runs Mermaid fence lint on **changed committed** Markdown and the SIGPIPE safety lint (split from `lint` so both halves run concurrently — issue #2080). Gitleaks is **not** skipped — its `--no-git` working-tree scan is documented in SECURITY.md as complementary to the dedicated `gitleaks` job's history scan. The `lint` job also runs on `push: main` (not just `pull_request`) so the pre-commit hook-env cache populates under the default-branch scope and fresh PRs read it warm (issue #1034). CI runs regression harnesses through the `test-harnesses` matrix (`make test-harnesses-1` through `make test-harnesses-20`) instead of one serial harness job. The `lint-bash32` hook runs under `make lint-only`, CI, and `python/cli.py checks run-relevant`; local `make lint` also runs `make lint-bash32` explicitly so untracked non-ignored shell files receive a whole-repo Bash 3.2 scan. Local `make lint` also runs the other direct static checks (readability preamble, renderer substitution safety, bare-grep probe, awk multibyte regex, codex exec auth, and SKILL.md flag signatures) between harnesses and pre-commit — it does **not** run `py-lint` or `py-test` (those stay explicit local targets and dedicated CI jobs). CI also runs separate dedicated jobs on top of the `lint` job: `shellcheck`, `agent-lint`, `agnix`, `gitleaks` (installs the same pinned engine and runs a full git-history scan on its own so the signal is independently re-runnable), `trufflehog` (CI-only; see "CI secret scanning" below), `python-lint` / `python-tests` as Python 3.11 jobs (`make py-lint` after installing `python/requirements-dev.txt` and Node for pyright; `make py-test` after installing `python/requirements-test.txt`), and `agent-sync` for internal invariants. The `agent-sync` job installs the same Python lint dependencies before running the topology-rule paths coverage check.
docs/linting.md:32:- **Relevant checks CLI (`python/cli.py checks run-relevant`)** — The Python dispatcher finds branch, staged, unstaged, and untracked changes; filters to existing regular files for `pre-commit run --files`; runs direct relevant make targets for touched domains; runs the contains-pin scanner; and attempts the full-repo `agent-lint` phase when available. If neither pre-commit, direct make targets, nor agent-lint runs, it exits 2 with an `ERROR: no validation phases ran ...` line instead of silently passing (issue #1276). The CLI does **not** run `npm ci` or otherwise install Node dependencies: when changed Markdown triggers `lint-mermaid-fences`, install repo devDependencies locally (for example `(cd mermaid-lint && npm ci)`) or skip that hook with `SKIP=lint-mermaid-fences` as in the Mermaid row above. Python tree changes (`python/*.py`, config files including `python/.pylintrc`, and requirements pins) run the direct `py-test` target only when `python3` is version 3.11 or newer and `python3 -m pytest` is available; they run the direct `py-lint` target only when `python3` is version 3.11 or newer and `ruff`, `pylint`, and `pyright` are already on `PATH`, leaving strict dependency installation to explicit `make py-lint` / `make py-test` and CI. `/implement` and `/review` use the CLI to capture verbose output under the session tmpdir and emit a one-line `RELEVANT_CHECKS_OK=true ...` green-path envelope when checks succeed. The default path fails closed on structural errors; `RELEVANT_CHECKS_SKIPPED=true` is reserved for explicit `--allow-skip` test paths. On failure, orchestrators read only `REDACTED_LOG_FILE` from the helper envelope. Hooks with `pass_filenames: false` (gitleaks) scan the full tree regardless of the scoped path argument — intentional so scoped checks cannot silently miss secrets outside the changed file set.

LARCH_SUMMARY_BEGIN
Split pyright into its own CI job, force `PYLINT_JOBS=0` only in the CI `python-lint` job, and leave local Makefile behavior unchanged.
LARCH_SUMMARY_END
LARCH_PLAN_BEGIN
## Approach

- Update CI only.
- Keep local `make py-lint` unchanged.
- Keep `python-lint-duplicate-code` untouched.
- Make jobs run in parallel by default:
  - `python-lint`: ruff + pylint only.
  - `python-pyright`: pyright only.
- Set `PYLINT_JOBS=0` at the `python-lint` job level so GitHub-hosted Linux uses all available cores.
- Remove `actions/setup-node` from `python-lint`.
- Add `actions/setup-node` to the new `python-pyright` job.
- Keep `python/requirements-dev.txt` installation in both jobs to avoid dependency reshaping.

## Files to modify/create

### UPDATED: .github/workflows/ci.yaml

- In `python-lint`:
  - Add job-level `env:`.
  - Set `PYLINT_JOBS: "0"`.
  - Add a short comment that CI forces all pylint workers while the Makefile fallback remains local behavior.
  - Remove the `actions/setup-node@v5` step.
  - Replace `run: make py-lint` with an inline ruff + pylint command:

```yaml
        run: |
          cd python
          ruff check .
          pylint -j "$PYLINT_JOBS" .
```

- Add a sibling `python-pyright` job near `python-lint`:
  - Use `ubuntu-latest`.
  - Keep the same 10 minute timeout.
  - Use the same Python 3.11 matrix shape as `python-lint`.
  - Checkout the repo.
  - Run `actions/setup-python@v6` with the same pip cache settings.
  - Run `actions/setup-node@v5`.
  - Install `python/requirements-dev.txt`.
  - Run:

```yaml
        run: cd python && pyright
```

## Edge cases

- Branch protection may still require only the old `python-lint` status.
  - Add the new `python-pyright` status check in GitHub settings outside this repo.
  - Otherwise pyright failures may stop blocking merges.
- Keep commands rooted in `python/`.
  - This preserves `.pylintrc` and `pyrightconfig.json` lookup behavior.
- Do not split ruff into its own job.
  - It is too fast to justify a new job.
- Do not touch `python-lint-duplicate-code`.
  - Its single-process pylint mode is intentional.

## Failure modes

- YAML indentation errors can break the workflow.
- If `PYLINT_JOBS=0` behaves unexpectedly on the runner, `python-lint` may fail instead of speeding up.
- If branch protection is not updated, coverage still runs in CI but may not gate merges.

## Testing strategy

- Run `make lint`.
- If available locally, run `actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yaml` for faster workflow-shape feedback.
- Validate on CI:
  - `python-lint` should no longer run pyright.
  - `python-pyright` should run and fail independently on type errors.
  - `python-lint` should complete in about half or less of the prior 166s wall time.
  - Combined coverage must still include ruff, full pylint, duplicate-code pylint, pyright, and tests.
